verdict.rationale: The RTX 5070 family page points developers to GPU-optimized SDKs and PyTorch backends on RTX AI PCs. The CUDA Toolkit page documents a compiler, runtime and libraries for deploying on desktop workstations, and the community cites the card's CUDA core count. However, no CUDA documentation in the pack explicitly lists the RTX 5070 Ti, or its Blackwell compute capability, as a supported target. missing for 10: explicit CUDA supported-GPU/compute-capability listing naming the RTX 5070 Ti, minimum toolkit/driver version for Blackwell consumer parts, hands-on corroboration of CUDA compute workloads on this card.

support.subject: As a developer, I can ship GPU-compute workloads on the vendor's toolchain — CUDA or ROCm/HIP documentation lists this part as a supported target

citations.quote: Access curated, GPU-optimized SDKs and models, and maximize performance across Windows ML, Ollama, PyTorch, and other inference backends
The toolkit includes GPU-accelerated libraries, debugging and optimization tools, a C/C++ compiler, and a runtime library.
With it, you can develop, optimize, and deploy your applications on GPU-accelerated embedded systems, desktop workstations, enterprise data centers, cloud-based platforms, and supercomputers.
